They share the same structure – `?i - item` – indicating that `?i` is an item. The core difference lies in the state they are in. One represents an item hidden, and the other represents an item worshipped. While they represent different actions (take_gold_pot_and_hide and worship_kettle_as_saint), the underlying concept of an item in a specific state is shared.  Merging them would simplify the domain by reducing redundancy.  We can represent this combined state with a new predicate that captures the general concept of an item being in a particular state, without specifying the exact action that led to that state. This avoids potential complexity when defining operators that might affect both 'concealed' and 'worshipped' items.
